input: According to NASA FLEX research (NASA/CR-2017-219502), what happens to the flame when ventilation velocity is near zero in microgravity?
context: [NASA/CR-2017-219502 | DOI:10.60555/mbq8-0451] FLEX on the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack observed spherical droplet combustion of liquid alkanes (heptane, octane) and alcohols (methanol). Liquid droplets burn via the d-square law. At droplet diameters between 0.8 mm and 1.5 mm, visible hot flames extinguished due to radiative heat loss, followed by low-temperature quasi-steady 'cool flame' burning undetectable in visual wavelengths. Disruption occurs when bubbles nucleate inside multi-component droplets.
target: Based on NASA FLEX findings (NASA/CR-2017-219502), under quiescent microgravity conditions (forced flow < 0.02 m/s), flames cannot sustain steady combustion and tend to self-extinguish. This occurs because without natural buoyancy, combustion products accumulate spherically around the reaction zone, causing localized oxygen starvation.

input: Explain to a high-school physics student why gravity changes the shape of a flame based on NASA FLEX studies.
context: [NASA/CR-2017-219502] FLEX on the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack observed spherical droplet combustion of liquid alkanes (heptane, octane) and alcohols (methanol). Liquid droplets burn via the d-square law. At droplet diameters between 0.8 mm and 1.5 mm, visible hot flames extinguished due to radiative heat loss, followed by low-temperature quasi-steady 'cool flame' burning undetectable in visual wavelengths. Disruption occurs when bubbles nucleate inside multi-component droplets.
target: On Earth, hot air is lighter than cold air, so buoyancy pulls hot gases upward into a familiar teardrop flame. In space (microgravity), there is no buoyancy. As NASA FLEX (NASA/CR-2017-219502) observed, heat only moves outward via slow molecular diffusion, creating a rounded, spherical flame. Without airflow, it suffocates in its own exhaust gases.

input: What is the exact flame height of titanium alloy bolts burning inside the Lunar Starship cabin at 8.0 psi?
context: Context provides records for PMMA, SIBAL, Nomex, and liquid droplets.
target: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE: The available NASA microgravity combustion archives (BASS-II, Saffire, FLEX, SoFIE) do not contain experimental flammability or flame height measurements for titanium alloy bolts under the specified conditions. NASA protocols forbid extrapolating polymer combustion models to metallic structural fires without empirical hot-particle testing.
